<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/">Includes, ownership and secrets</a><span class="nv-section-count">11</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One ordered stream where later wins and every override is recorded — over files nobody but the runtime account may write.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#include-takes-a-path-or-a-dir"><code>[[include]]</code> takes a <code>path</code> or a <code>dir</code>, never both and never neither, and a <code>dir</code> is not a glob</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#an-include-cycle-is-refused-and-nesting-is-capped-at-eight">An include cycle is refused with the chain named, and nesting past eight is refused as depth</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#later-wins-and-every-override-is-recorded">The tree is one ordered stream, a later assignment wins, and every override is recorded with both origins</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#a-value-array-replaces-and-a-table-appends">A value array is replaced wholesale by a later file; <code>[[table]]</code> entries accumulate across the tree</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#a-relative-path-resolves-against-the-file-it-is-written-in">A relative path resolves against the directory of the file it is written in; a command-line path against the working directory</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#any-file-in-the-tree-may-set-any-directive">Any file in the tree may set any directive, <code>System</code> class included</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#ownership-is-the-trust-boundary">Every file the configuration reads, and its directory, must be owned by the runtime account or root and writable by nobody else</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#the-ownership-check-runs-where-it-can-be-answered">The ownership check runs on <code>nvs serve</code> and on reload; <code>nvs run</code>, <code>config check</code> and <code>config dump</code> read without it, and an unchecked file can grant nothing</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#optional-covers-absence-and-moves-the-check-to-the-directory"><code>optional = true</code> covers absence and nothing else, and an absent include is checked at the directory that would hold it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#a-secret-is-a-file-whose-content-is-the-value">A secret directive has a <code>_file</code> sibling, exactly one of the pair is set, and the file's whole content is the value</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/includes-and-ownership/#a-secret-file-is-checked-for-integrity-and-advised-on-exposure">A secret file another account can write refuses the boot; one another account can read only warns</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/">Changeability classes</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">The file states defaults, not ceilings. Three classes decide what a running request may change, and a refusal is never a clamp.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#one-parser-for-the-boot-path-and-config-set">The boot path and <code>Core\Config::set</code> parse a value through one configuration is one immutable snapshot a request clones at start, and a reload replaces it whole after validating everything</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#three-changeability-classes"><code>nvs.toml</code> states defaults, not ceilings, and every directive carries one of three changeability classes</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#a-directive-flag-is-a-closed-list-at-the-global-layer">A CLI flag that sets a directive is one of a closed list, wins over every file, and there is no <code>--set</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#reloadability-is-its-own-field">Reloadability is a second registry field, <code>Reload</code> or <code>Boot</code>, orthogonal to the changeability class</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#ceilings-are-their-own-directives">A ceiling is a <code>System</code> directive with the default's key name, and <code>false</code> removes it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#system-means-a-request-may-not-set-it">A directive is <code>System</code> when changing it from inside a request would affect something other than that data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#a-refused-set-returns-false">A refused <code>Core\Config::set</code> returns <code>false</code> and leaves the value unchanged; it is never clamped</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/changeability-classes/#ini-set-is-core-config-set"><code>ini_set</code> is <section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/">Reloading and control</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">An edit reaches the next request without a restart, and the running process is controlled over one local socket and no network surface.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#an-edit-reaches-the-next-request-without-a-restart">A source change reaches the next request in every mode: every file a program reached is checked in the background, and a change is compiled whole from a quiet tree before one pointer swap</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#a-request-keeps-the-unit-it-resolved">A file is resolved once per isolate, so an edit is invisible to a request already running</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#a-broken-edit-fails-the-requests-that-resolve-it">A revalidated file that no longer compiles fails the requests that resolve it afterwards, loudly, and the last good version is never served in its place</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#a-reload-names-what-it-could-not-apply">A reload reports what it applied, names every changed <code>Boot</code> key it could not apply, and counts the units it invalidated</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#one-local-control-socket">The server is controlled over one local socket whose owner and mode are the authentication, and <code>nvs ctl</code> is its client</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#no-network-control-surface">There is no network-reachable control surface, in either direction of configuration</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#ctl-config-reports-the-live-snapshot"><code>nvs ctl config</code> reports what the running process actually holds, including an optional include that appeared after boot</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/reloading-and-control/#check-and-dump-audit-the-tree-offline"><code>nvs config check</code> and <code>nvs config dump</code> resolve the tree with no server, and <code>dump --origin</code> names where every value came from</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/">Run modes</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Exactly two, defaulting to production, selected by the file or a flag and never by an environment variable.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/#two-modes-and-the-default-is-production">A run mode is one of exactly two closed values, and with nothing configured it is <code>production</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/#the-mode-flag-wins-over-the-file">The mode a server starts in comes from <code>nvs.toml</code> or from <code>nvs serve --mode=</code>, and the flag is the last word</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/#no-environment-variable-selects-the-mode">No environment variable selects the run mode — not <code>NVS_MODE</code>, not <code>APP_ENV</code>, not <code>NODE_ENV</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/#a-mode-is-five-defaults">A mode is a shorthand for the defaults of five <code>Runtime</code> directives, and governs nothing else</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/#a-startup-default-is-never-flipped">A mode also selects three startup defaults, chosen when a configuration is published, never re-derived by a mode flip, and never flippable from code</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/run-modes/#a-program-may-read-and-flip-its-mode">A program may read the mode and may flip it for its own request, bounded by a <code>System</code> ceiling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/">Application blocks</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">An application is its entry file path. A mount routes; an <code>[[app]]</code> block sets policy, bounded by the global ceiling.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/#an-application-is-its-entry-file-path">An application is its entry file path, and an <code>[[app]]</code> block is keyed on a <code>root</code> directory or one <code>entry</code> file</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/#app-keys-are-canonicalized-before-matching">Both sides of an <code>[[app]]</code> match are canonicalized first, and a key naming nothing examinable refuses the boot</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/#origin-is-a-block-key-and-there-is-no-app-table"><code>origin</code> and <code>mode</code> sit on the <code>[[app]]</code> block itself, and there is no global <code>[app]</code> table</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/#every-matching-app-block-applies-least-specific-first">Every matching <code>[[app]]</code> block applies, least-specific <code>root</code> first, and two blocks on one canonical path are a duplicate</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/#an-app-block-may-widen-bounded-by-the-global-ceiling">An <code>[[app]]</code> block may widen a limit or grant a capability up to the global ceiling, and may only lower its own ceiling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/application-blocks/#a-mount-routes-and-an-app-block-sets-policy">A <code>[[server.mount]]</code> routes and carries no <code>mode</code>; an <code>[[app]]</code> block sets policy</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/scheduled-work/">Scheduled work</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A config block, not a runtime API: five cron fields, a mandatory scope, a lease across a fleet, and a missed fire that stays missed.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/scheduled-work/#scheduled-work-is-a-config-block">Scheduled work is a <code>[[schedule]]</code> entry firing a <code>spawn script</code>, <h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/">Stores, sockets and the compiled-unit cache</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Where a Unix socket may be written, why the extension set is in every cache key, and which opcache directives an operator alone owns.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store">A store an operator configured is authorized by the configuring — title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#unix-scheme-in-a-url-and-a-bare-path-in-a-host">A socket is <code>unix:</code> where the key is a URL and a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#a-unix-spelling-with-no-af-unix-transport-refuses-at-boot">A Unix spelling on a build with no <code>AF_UNIX</code> transport is refused at boot, never read as loopback TCP</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#net-local-is-named-and-not-on-the-roster">A program-supplied socket path needs <code>net.local</code>, a path-scoped grant carrying no address policy and governing both ends</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#the-extension-set-is-in-every-unit-key">The extension set is folded into one <code>env_hash</code> that both compiled-unit cache keys carry, so an extension change is an ordinary cache miss</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#opcache-revalidation-is-system-class"><code>opcache.validate</code>, its rate cap and <code>opcache.settle</code> are <code>System</code>, class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#opcache-file-cache-directives-are-system">The five <code>opcache.file_cache*</code> directives are <code>System</code>-class, because where compiled code is read from is a code-injection primitive</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/config/stores-and-caches/#telemetry-and-update-endpoints-are-configuration">The update-check and telemetry
